title: The New Friends of Rhythm sides for International
summary: Sylvan Shulman's group, studio musicians with advanced, odd arrangements; date probably 1947.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And by way of contracts, again, some time according to the information I have, either later that year or some time in 1947 -- nobody seems to know for sure what the exact date was -- you went back and made a recording with strings again.
Yeah.
This is the Sylvan Shulman date with a group he called "The New Friends of Rhythm."
Yes. There was -- what, International label, I believe? Is that International?
Yes, and it has six sides.
Yes. I guess they just thought about me. So they called me up and arranged this -- The International Recording Company was a little outfit. And I think they operated out of Schirmer's.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Out of where?

Schirmer's, the music house. And the New Friends of Rhythm, of course, they had been putting stuff together. And this group of selections came up as a tenth anniversary album.-- Maxine Sullivan's Tenth Anniversary Album.
Oh, I see. So in other words, the recording date is more likely to be 1947.
That's right, '47. I have a copy of this, but I guess it's three it's a three record album.
Yes. Three 78's.
That's right, three 78's. And the cover is Maxine Sullivan's Tenth Anniversary Album. So that would be 1947.
So that sort of introduced me to the International Company. Then I was invited back to do the selections that came later with Ellis Larkins. See, they're all International.
There's a slightly kind of
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
classical flavor to the string accompaniment from these sides of The New Friends of Rhythm.
Yes. They're kind of weird. I mean, when you listen to them. They were strange by comparison. As you'll notice --
A little advanced for that time.
That's right.
Self-conciously so. I mean were they striving to be avant garde or...
I don't think so. I guess -- well they called themselves The New Friends of Rhythm -- this is the style that they were trying to create.
And they had been doing somethings --
(End of Tape 2A)
I just want to add a short footnote.
The ASCAP boycott of the radio networks begun in January 1941. The A.F. of M. ban on recording started in August of 1942 and lasted for
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
about a year. It varied from different record companies.
They had been doing some things on their own. They were studio musicians, and they were creating a style -- you know, The New Friends of Rhythm.

I thought they were very modern. The arrangements were sort of strange, maybe because as you'll notice, lot of the things like "If I Had A Ribbon Bos, "Lock Lochman and "Jackie Boy," they're entirely different arrangements altogether.
Yes.
And I found my way in and out in the cracks.
It was quite an experience, because Hank D'Amico, the terrific clarinetist, and I would follow--- I knew what he was trying to do. I really didn't know the other members of the group too well.
We had to rehearse quite a bit. Of
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
course, all I had to do was sing the melody. They were doing all the strange things behind me. I did what I was -- But it was sort of strange hearing the different changes that I hadn't been used to.
